case.label: // CASE STUDY — 001
case.headline: E-Commerce Platform: Zero to 99.9% Uptime
case.p1: A growing e-commerce client ran on a single VPS: manual SSH deploys, no monitoring, and nightly backups no one had ever restored. Releases caused 20–30 minute outages during business hours, and a disk-full incident had already taken the store down once.
case.p2: Over three weeks I rebuilt the platform around clear failure domains — containerized every service, moved state onto a replicated Postgres and Redis layer, and put the stack behind an HA Nginx pair on a Proxmox cluster. A GitLab pipeline replaced hand-run deploys with tested, blue-green releases and one-command rollback.
case.p3: Eight months on: zero unplanned downtime, deploys down from 45 minutes to 90 seconds, and a recovery path that has actually been tested. Infrastructure cost landed ~38% below the equivalent managed-cloud setup.
case.decision_1: Proxmox HA over managed cloud — kept full control and cut infra cost ~38%, accepting ownership of the hardware lifecycle as the tradeoff.
case.decision_2: Blue-green releases over rolling updates — instant, atomic rollback was worth the extra capacity held during each deploy.
case.decision_3: Self-hosted Prometheus + Loki over a hosted APM — lower cost and full data ownership; alerts fire on symptoms users feel, not raw CPU.
case.tl_problem_desc: A single VPS, manual SSH deploys, and zero monitoring — every release risked a 30-minute outage during business hours.
case.tl_architecture_desc: Mapped a layered, highly-available design: CDN edge, load-balanced app tier, and a replicated data layer with clear failure domains.
case.tl_infrastructure_desc: Provisioned a Proxmox HA cluster with ZFS storage pools, containerized every service, and codified it all with Ansible & Terraform.
case.tl_networking_desc: Nginx HA reverse proxy with SSL termination, rate limiting, and a Cloudflare edge for DDoS protection and global caching.
case.tl_deployment_desc: A GitOps CI/CD pipeline: push to main → tested, built, and rolled out with zero-downtime blue-green releases in under 90 seconds.
case.tl_operations_desc: Full observability with Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting — plus hourly snapshots and a tested disaster-recovery plan.
case.tl_monitoring_desc: Full observability with Prometheus, Grafana, and alerting rules — issues are caught and paged before users ever notice.
case.tl_scaling_desc: Auto-scaling with load balancing and hourly snapshots — traffic spikes are absorbed automatically and recovery is one tested command away.
projects.label: // DEPLOYED SYSTEMS
projects.headline: Featured Project
projects.subtitle: One system, built end to end and running in production — not a portfolio demo.
projects.lf_tagline: Log management for servers that actually fill up.
projects.lf_desc: A self-hosted log dashboard for teams who need to read production logs without handing out SSH access — then reclaim the disk those logs ate. It deletes log lines older than a date you pick, from inside the files, instead of dropping whole files. Every action is attributed: who deleted what, when, and from which IP.
projects.lf_f1_d: Pick a date, preview how many lines and megabytes it frees, confirm twice. Parses nginx, PHP, and syslog timestamp formats; undated continuation lines follow the entry above them.
projects.lf_f2_d: Tails the last N lines instead of loading the file, with ERROR / WARN / INFO colouring and search-term highlighting.
projects.lf_f3_d: Full-file analysis runs as a detached CLI worker — no request timeouts. Progress and results live in one JSON the page polls.
projects.lf_f4_d: Login, view, download, delete, cleanup, and settings changes are all recorded with user and IP. Admins see everyone; viewers see only themselves.
projects.lf_f5_d: SMTP alerts spoken over raw sockets with TLS, outbound webhooks, and a token-authenticated REST API for status, files, reads, and audit.
projects.lf_f6_d: Several named log directories as tabs, roles split into admin and viewer, bcrypt passwords, CSRF-guarded forms, and a full Arabic / English UI with RTL.
projects.lf_note: Running in production on a client's pharmacy-chain infrastructure since 2026.
